claim.natural: The least n such that every red-blue edge-colouring of K_n contains two pairwise vertex-disjoint monochromatic copies of K_4 is 20; the two copies may have different colours.

limitations: The upper bound reuses the parent z(20)=6 candidate's two-core reduction, Ramsey-core catalogue, exact CNFs, and DRUP/LRAT proof objects rather than independently reproducing them.
Certificate checks establish unsatisfiability only for the two exact CNFs.
The catalogue implementation, nauty canonicalisation, graph-to-CNF implementation, operating system, compiler, file I/O, and hardware are not formally verified.
The inherited result remains an unrefereed candidate with no reported complete human review or independent reproduction.
dependencies.statement: The inherited fixed-core result establishes that, after selecting a first monochromatic K_4 in a colouring of K_20, neither of the two possible 16-vertex (4,4)-Ramsey cores admits a 64-cross-edge extension avoiding a second vertex-disjoint monochromatic K_4. This is exactly the upper-bound property needed for VR_2(K_4)≤20.

downstream.statement: May be cited or investigated only as an unrefereed candidate determination of VR_2(K_4)=20, not as an authenticated established theorem. State that the two copies may differ in colour; the 19-vertex lower construction is hand-checkable with a standard-library verifier; the upper bound reuses the parent fixed-core candidate; certificate checking covers only the exact CNFs; the graph-to-CNF bridge is separate and not formalized end to end; no complete human review, independent reproduction, extremal uniqueness or enumeration, or complete objection search is supplied.
